images.title: Squares ending in 1, and numbers that never are squares
images.purpose: Shows two squares that end in 1 because their numbers end in 1 or 9, beside five numbers ruled out as squares by their last digit.
images.composition: Plain white background, the main object large and centred with wide empty margins, no scenery, no characters, no extra decoration. Two groups side by side with a wide gap: two equation cards on the left, five number cards on the right.
images.exact_structure: Left group: exactly 2 cards stacked, reading 31² = 961 and 39² = 1521; on each card the last digit of the number being squared (the 1 of 31 and the 9 of 39) and the final 1 of the answer are coloured teal (#0072B2), everything else dark. Right group: exactly 5 cards in a row reading 52, 73, 107, 218 and 1003; on each card the last digit (2, 3, 7, 8, 3) is coloured vermilion (#D55E00) and the rest is dark. Under the right group: never squares. Nothing else in the frame.
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
images.takeaway: A number ending in 1 or 9 has a square ending in 1, and a number ending in 2, 3, 7 or 8 is never a square.
images.description: Shows two squares that end in 1 because their numbers end in 1 or 9, beside five numbers ruled out as squares by their last digit.

image_decisions.why: Putting the coloured last digits side by side shows how the units digit alone predicts or rules out a square.
